playbook:
When I hold K and I'm first to act or the opponent checks to me, I bet for value and to apply pressure.

When I hold Q and I'm first to act, I default to checking for pot control in neutral-stack situations; I switch to a bet when the opponent is short-stacked or the table dynamics favor stealing.

When I hold Q and the opponent bets a single chip, I call — Q has enough showdown equity to contest small bets unless stack dynamics or previous info signal a very strong hand.

When I hold J and I'm first to act in a small/neutral-stack situation, I check to control the pot and avoid low-equity bluffs.

When I hold J and I'm behind in chips but not catastrophically short, I will sometimes open with a bet to apply pressure and attempt a steal; I will not make this my default — use it selectively rather than frequently.

When the opponent checks to me and I have a marginal hand (J or Q), I bet to try to steal only if my stack position or opponent tendencies make aggression likely profitable; otherwise check.

When the opponent bets after my check and I hold J or Q and the bet is small relative to the stacks, I call to see showdown; fold only to larger bets or clear evidence of K.

When facing bets, prioritize calling small (one-chip) bets with Q or J for showdown equity; fold when the bet size or history implies I am heavily dominated.

Always declare my actual card at showdown; never misdeclare.
